# Commit identity: what init reports and records, and which identity the
# committing commands apply. The scenario names the identity through GIT_CONFIG_*
# environment entries, which outrank the machine's system and global
# configuration, so no host configuration takes part.

env GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2
env GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=user.name
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=ada
env GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=user.email
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=ada@example.com

# An identity git config names belongs to the machine: init reports it, applies
# it to the init commit, and writes nothing into akb.yaml.
exec akb init cfg-kb
stdout '^commit identity: from git config \(ada <ada@example\.com>\) — not recorded; each machine''s git identity applies$'
! grep 'git-author' cfg-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
! grep 'git-email' cfg-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
exec git -C cfg-kb log -1 --format='%an <%ae>'
stdout '^ada <ada@example\.com>$'

# An identity no source names falls back to the akb default, which init records
# so that a clone to a machine without an identity can still commit.
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=
exec akb init default-kb
stdout '^commit identity: agent-kb <agent@agent-kb> \(default — no git identity found; recorded in akb\.yaml, edit git-author/git-email to change\)$'
grep '^git-author: agent-kb$' default-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
grep '^git-email: agent@agent-kb$' default-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
exec git -C default-kb log -1 --format='%an <%ae>'
stdout '^agent-kb <agent@agent-kb>$'

# A complete flag pair is the identity the invoker declares for the base: it is
# recorded in akb.yaml, attributes the init commit, and outranks every ambient
# source.
exec akb init flag-kb --author-name 'Grace Hopper' --author-email grace@example.com
stdout '^commit identity: from --author-name/--author-email \(Grace Hopper <grace@example\.com>\) — recorded in akb\.yaml, edit git-author/git-email to change$'
grep '^git-author: Grace Hopper$' flag-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
grep '^git-email: grace@example\.com$' flag-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
exec git -C flag-kb log -1 --format='%an <%ae>'
stdout '^Grace Hopper <grace@example\.com>$'

# A partial pair is ambient for the field the flag left out — here git config
# fills the email — so nothing is recorded and the flag applies to the init
# commit alone.
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=ada
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=ada@example.com
exec akb init partial-kb --author-name 'Grace Hopper'
stdout '^commit identity: from --author-name alone \(Grace Hopper <ada@example\.com>\) — not recorded; only a complete --author-name/--author-email pair is recorded in akb\.yaml; later commits use each machine''s identity$'
! grep 'git-author' partial-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
! grep 'git-email' partial-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
exec git -C partial-kb log -1 --format='%an <%ae>'
stdout '^Grace Hopper <ada@example\.com>$'

# An unversioned base never commits, so the flags have nothing to attribute:
# no identity is resolved, reported, or recorded.
exec akb init plain-kb --no-git --author-name 'Grace Hopper' --author-email grace@example.com
! stdout 'commit identity'
! grep 'git-author' plain-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml
! grep 'git-email' plain-kb/.agent-kb/akb.yaml

cd default-kb
exec akb template get note --full --examples
cp stdout .agent-kb/templates/note.yaml

# The environment outranks what the base records.
env AKB_AUTHOR_NAME=env-ada
env AKB_AUTHOR_EMAIL=env-ada@example.com
stdin ../note-input.md
exec akb write notes/env-note.md
stdout '^Written to kb/notes/env-note\.md$'
exec git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>'
stdout '^env-ada <env-ada@example\.com>$'

# What the base records outranks git-native resolution: the ambient
# configuration still names ada, and the commit is attributed to the base.
env AKB_AUTHOR_NAME=
env AKB_AUTHOR_EMAIL=
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=ada
env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=ada@example.com
stdin ../note-input.md
exec akb write notes/cfg-note.md
stdout '^Written to kb/notes/cfg-note\.md$'
exec git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>'
stdout '^agent-kb <agent@agent-kb>$'

-- note-input.md --
---
type: note
title: Identity note
summary: Note written to check the commit identity
tags: identity
---
A page whose commit records the identity the invocation resolved.
